newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union workers step up threat of strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union workers step up threat of strike.

text.p: Militant South Korean workers and activist students on Saturday renewed their threat of an all-out strike later this month if a controversial new labour law is not repealed.

"We want the bill revoked. We will launch an all-out strike unless our demands are met," Hur Young-ku, a leader of the outlawed Korean Federation of Trade Unions, told about 500 people at a rally in a Seoul plaza.

On Thursday, the confederation said it had postponed a strike from February 18 to between February 24 and 28 to see what parliament does to the new law, which makes it easier for employers to lay off workers and fire strikers.
The National Assembly agreed to reconvene on February 17 for a 30-day session to discuss the possible revision of the law and the scandal over the troubled Hanbo Steel Co.
Massive strikes began in late December after the the ruling New Korea Party rammed the labour law through parliament at an early morning session at which the opposition was not present.
The protesters on Saturday also accused the government of trying to cover up the Hanbo scandal by prematurely ending their investigation.
"People don't believe the investigation is enough. Prosecutors should begin the probe again," said Kwon Jin-kwan, a Sungkonghoe University professor invited to speak at the rally.

On Friday, state prosecutors said their three-week probe into a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo was winding down with several of President Kim's closest political allies and top bankers in custody.
But opposition parties and newspapers charged that the prosecution had failed to ferret out the top people behind the crisis, which involved massive loans to the failed Hanbo Steel.
